meta.title: Bangkok Transport Guide 2026: Grab, Bolt, Trains & MuvMi Explained
meta.desc: Complete guide to getting around Bangkok in 2026. Grab vs Bolt comparison table, MuvMi electric tuk-tuks, and train payment guide (BTS/MRT credit card touch). Avoid scams like a local.

hero.title: Bangkok Transport Guide
hero.subtitle: Master the City Like a Local

intro.p1:
"Taxi won't use the meter" "Tuk-tuk driver wants 300 baht for a 2-minute ride..."
Transport stress can be eliminated with the right apps and knowledge.
intro.p2:
Bangkok is actually the most app-advanced city in Southeast Asia for transport.
Book rides at fair prices, skip traffic jams with trains, and use electric tuk-tuks for short hops.
Master the '3 Essential Tools (Grab/Bolt/MuvMi)' and 'train payment tricks' used by residents, and your Bangkok life will become truly liberated.

grabBolt.title: Ride Apps: Grab vs Bolt
grabBolt.desc: No more flagging down street taxis. With these two apps, you can get anywhere safely—even without speaking the language or carrying cash.

advice.title: Pro Strategy
advice.text: 【Best Practice】Start with cheap "Bolt." If no cars available, switch to "Grab." This "dual-app" approach is optimal.

muvmi.title: Short Distance MVP: MuvMi
muvmi.desc:
"Too hot to walk from the station to my condo..."
This is where MuvMi, an electric tuk-tuk share service, shines. It covers major areas like Phrom Phong and Ari.

train.title: Traffic-Free Trains (BTS / MRT)
train.desc:
To avoid Bangkok's infamous traffic, trains are your best bet.
However, "payment methods differ by line"—important to know.

mrt.name: MRT (Subway)
mrt.desc: Tap your VISA/Mastercard directly at the gate. Zero wait at ticket counters.
mrt.tips: ※ Just tap your VISA Touch-enabled card

bts.name: BTS (Skytrain)
bts.desc: Unfortunately, no direct credit card payment. Buying tickets every time is annoying, so get the "Rabbit Card" IC card.
bts.tips: ※ Say "Rabbit Card, please" at the station counter (passport required, 100B fee + top-up)

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Q. Do I need to tip taxi drivers?
faq.a1: A. Generally no, but rounding up a few baht or giving 20 THB for helping with luggage is polite.
faq.q2: Q. Can I ride public buses?
faq.a2: A. Yes, but routes are complex and many buses have no AC—challenging for beginners. Master trains and ride apps first.
faq.q3: Q. Are motorcycle taxis (orange vests) safe?
faq.a3: A. Great for beating traffic but higher accident risk. Always wear a helmet and book via Grab/Bolt bike feature to avoid fare disputes.

cta.title: Prepare Before You Leave Home.
cta.desc:
Grab and Bolt require SMS verification, so download and register in your home country.
Then enjoy seamless transport from day one in Bangkok.
